_comment: Spec 108 D39 (T148): the agent-facing TOOL refusals of a profile's tool policy, byte-for-byte after substituting <server>, <tool>, <tier> (the tool's tier), <cap> ("read" or "read and write") and <label>. `disclosed` is what a caller whose effective profile is its OWN gets (source pin, binding, url or session): it names the profile. `undisclosed` is what every other caller gets (source anonymous: naming the operator's anonymous_profile would hand it to any local process; a dangling or out-of-scope shape is non-disclosing and unchanged) and is byte-identical to the pre-D39 text. <label> is `"<title>" (<slug>)` with the title rendered by Go %q, or `"<slug>"` alone when the title is empty or equals the slug. Readers: TestProfileToolPolicyRefusal_MatchesToolRefusalsGolden and the MCP, REST and CLI tests in internal/server, internal/httpapi and cmd/mcpproxy. The four ADMIN refusals live in refusals.json and are untouched.

refusals.name: tier
refusals.disclosed: blocked by profile: <server>:<tool> is a <tier> tool; profile <label> allows <cap> tools only
refusals.undisclosed: blocked by profile: <server>:<tool> is a <tier> tool; this profile allows <cap> tools only

refusals.name: rule
refusals.disclosed: blocked by profile: <server>:<tool> is denied by a rule in profile <label>
refusals.undisclosed: blocked by profile: <server>:<tool> is denied by a profile rule

refusals.name: unannotated
refusals.disclosed: blocked by profile: <server>:<tool> has no tier annotation; an operator can classify it in profile <label> to allow it
refusals.undisclosed: blocked by profile: <server>:<tool> has no tier annotation; an operator can classify it in the profile to allow it
